title: Tension rises between the U.S. and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz and oil prices rise
summary: Iran denies extending the ceasefire, Washington attacks a cargo ship bound for Iran, and Trump asserts control of the strait, while crude oil rebounds on fears of a blockade.

title: U.S. inflation stands at 3.4% and the New York Stock Exchange closes mixed: Dow falls, Nasdaq rises
summary: The July CPI matched expectations and reinforced bets on an interest rate cut, boosting tech stocks, while the Dow posted its third decline due to Middle East uncertainty.

title: Japan's corporate price index rises 7.2% year-on-year in July
summary: Producer inflation stays above 7% for a second consecutive month, though its pace of increase has slowed slightly.

title: Four candidates vie for the Kagawa governorship, with the incumbent seeking reelection
summary: The evaluation of the acting governor's performance is the focus of the campaign ahead of the vote on the 30th.

title: NBA's Lakers sold for more than $12.5 billion, a record in sports
summary: The buyer includes businessman Kushner and the former CEO of Disney, in the largest deal for a sports team in history.

title: Two two-meter pythons escape from an apartment in Kawasaki
summary: The snakes fled through the balcony while the owner slept, and authorities are searching for the animals in the Tama district.

title: Law penalizing damage to the national flag takes effect in Japan amid criticism over freedom of expression
summary: The rule, which punishes damaging the national emblem, was criticized for the risk of restricting freedom of expression and being interpreted broadly.

title: Hiroshi Okuda, former Toyota president, dies and receives tributes in Japan
summary: The former executive, a driver of Toyota's global expansion and the Aichi Expo, died and prompted expressions of condolence from authorities and the business world.

title: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt leaves her post
summary: The youngest press secretary in U.S. history resigns to spend more time with her children and family, according to Trump.

title: Nikkei index on Tokyo Stock Exchange rises sharply and recovers the 68,000-point level
summary: The advance of U.S. technology stocks boosted the Japanese market, which briefly exceeded 68,700 points.

title: A total solar eclipse darkens Europe and is visible in Iceland for the first time in six centuries
summary: Thousands of people followed the phenomenon with special glasses, and hotel prices soared, in one of the year's biggest astronomical events.

title: Magnitude 7.4 earthquake in Colombia surpasses 260 dead
summary: Rescue teams continue searching for survivors as the critical 72-hour period after the quake approaches.

title: Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak with ideal conditions in Japan
summary: The absence of the moon favored observation during the nights of August 12 and 13, with clear skies in some regions.

title: Trump is sued over new paid-posts service
summary: Several media outlets allege that the platform restricts equal access to the president's accounts and call it an unprecedented and corrupt measure.

title: Japan considers a system to limit the number of foreign residents
summary: Measures to tighten immigration policy raise concerns about their impact on foreigners' rights and society.

title: Yen sits around 159 yen per dollar after intervention and U.S. CPI
summary: The Japanese currency rose slightly after the intervention, but selling pressure remained and the exchange rate hovered around 159 yen.

title: Zhu Rongji, former Chinese premier, dies at age 97
summary: The architect of China's economic opening and its entry into the WTO promoted deep market reforms during his tenure.

title: Sato and Morishita of the Hanshin Tigers star in intense battle for home run lead
summary: The two batters hit consecutive home runs against the Yomiuri Giants and fuel the fight for the home run title in Japan.

title: Japan renews the leadership of the Public Prosecutors Office: outgoing prosecutor general apologizes for scandals
summary: Naomi Unemoto left the post with a message of apology for the irregularities, while her successor takes over amid a climate of pressure.
